newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PDL ups full year profit forecasts.
newsitem.headline: PDL ups full year profit forecasts.

text.p: PDL Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday it now anticipates a full year tax-paid profit in the range of NZ$12.5 to $13 million, as a result of the net gain made on the acquisition of the minority interests in MasterTrade Group.
This compares with a forecasts made in September of a $12.4 million post-tax full year profit.
The company also said that during the next financial year it should see a significant increase in post-tax profitability and earnings per share.
This was due to the increased contribution from PDL Industries Australia, the restructuring of Master Trade and the improvement in PDL's Asian subsidiaries.

PDL said demand on its New Zealand manufacturing companies grew during the third quarter, increasing the production levels strongly. Its Australian subsidiary made good progress and was on track, the company said.
MasterTrade experienced margin erosion, with very strong competition within the electrical and plumbing wholesaling network.
"In Asia we are experiencing weaker demand for our fan products but our market shares in both electrical accessories and switchgear are improving with margins remaining firm," PDL said.

It said its net profit in the nine months to December 31 of NZ$9.4 million (against $10 million in the corresponding period), was slightly under its projections made in September of a full year post-tax profit of $12.4 million.
However, PDL said it was in a strong financial position and the predicted stronger returns in the second half were occurring.
"We are committed to our debt reduction programme in anticipation of higher interests rates in the medium term," it said.

PDL said the formal take-over process of the minority interest in MasterTrade Group Ltd was completed in December. MasterTrade has been de-listed from the NZSE and restructuring of the group had commenced.
PDL Industries Australia Pty Ltd continued to improve its market share in Australia and was expected to meet its profit targets for the year through to March 31.
Interest costs were 71 percent higher than the corresponding period last year due to higher rates and increased borrowings used to fund the purchase of minority interests in MasterTrade Group.
